Eight of nine variants in the founding cohort lie in the 198-nucleotide last coding exon, so truncating alleles are expected to escape nonsense-mediated decay and yield C-terminally altered protein. Mutant SPN1 fails to self-oligomerize and aggregates in the cytoplasm; other variants reduce importin-beta binding and impair folding. Total SPN1 abundance can be unchanged, so the defect is functional rather than a loss of protein.
